title: Computational Reconstruction of Pancreatic Islets as a Tool for Structural and Functional Analysis
protocol: Install IsletLab in Linux by following sections 2 and 3 of the Supplementary File 2 for Windows or macOS installation.
Open an internet browser and navigate to https://github.com/gjfelix/IsletLab.
Download and extract the IsletLab repository files.
Verify that gcc and nvcc compilers are installed using terminal commands: gcc --version and nvcc --version.
Follow instructions in section 1 of Supplementary File 2 if any compiler command is unrecognized.
Download and install the data science platform (see Table of Materials).
Open a terminal and navigate to the IsletLab folder.
Create a new environment by typing conda env create -f isletlabgui_v1.0.yml in the terminal.
Activate the new environment using: conda activate isletlab_v1.0
Launch the IsletLab application by typing python isletlabgui_v1.0.py in the terminal.
Prepare the input data for islet reconstruction.
Organize the input islet data in a four-column file.
Include cell type codes (11: ɑ-cell, 12: β-cell, 13: δ-cell) in column 1.
Enter x, y, and z coordinates in columns 2 to 4 respectively.
Ensure the input file does not include column headers.
Click the Load Initial Islet button.
Select the file containing input data.
Generate an initial islet, the 3D representation, and the corresponding statistics.
In case of error message 'Error loading islet file', repeat step 2.1.
Click the Reconstruction Settings button.
Modify the optimization parameters.
Set the initial temperature = 1.
Set the iterations factor = 1.
Set the acceptance factor = 1.
Click the OK button to save parameter values.
Increase the temperature, iterations, and acceptance factors for better reconstruction results at the expense of computing time.
Click the Reconstruct Islet button.
Open the reconstruction log window.
Click the Run button to start the reconstruction process.
Monitor the optimization process until the message 'Please close this window to continue' is displayed.
Close the reconstruction log window to generate the visual representation of the reconstructed islet and to calculate the related statistics.
Evaluate the results by analyzing the optimization statistics shown in the final islet tab of the statistics panel.
Focus on maximizing the percentage of experimental cells included in the reconstructed islets (% of experimental) or minimizing the number of overlaps.
If the % of experimental statistic is considered low according to user objectives, restart IsletLab and increase initial temperature, iterations factor, and acceptance factor.
Repeat steps 2.1-2.4 until satisfactory results are obtained (>95% of experimental cells).
Click the Reconstruction Settings button and set the Contact Tolerance parameter to define cell-to-cell contact tolerance.
Click OK to save the parameter values.
Click the Cell-to-Cell Contacts button in the interface to identify cells in close contact.
Increase (decrease) the contact tolerance parameter to increase (decrease) the number of cell-to-cell contacts.
Generate the islet network by clicking the Build Network button.
Switch to the Simulation Tab of the configuration panel for functional simulation of the reconstructed islet.
Select the desired mode of intrinsic frequency - Constant or Random.
Click the Configure Intrinsic Frequency button to define the oscillators' frequency (in Hz).
Define the mean and deviation (in Hz) for normally distributed random frequencies if a random intrinsic frequency is selected.
Select the desired mode of the initial phase - Constant or Random.
Click the Configure Initial Phase button to define the phase of the oscillators (in radians) if a constant initial phase is selected.
Assign random phases between 0 and 2π to all the oscillators if a random initial phase is selected.
Click the Configure Interactions button to define cell-to-cell interaction parameters in the interaction strength window.
Define the total simulation time, time step, and save factor (number of steps between saved data points).
Set the total time to 20000 s, with a time step of 0.1 s and a save factor of 500 for the simulation shown in Figure 5.
Define the number of blocks for the GPU simulation.
Set the number of threads per block according to the GPU's multiprocessors and cores.
Specify the computing platform capability based on the GPU hardware specifications.
Click the Run Simulation button to open the simulation log window.
Start the simulation by clicking the Run button in the simulation log window.
Monitor the simulation process until the legend 'Please close the window to continue' is displayed.
Close the simulation log window after the message appears.
Save the project file (optional) by selecting File > Export Project from the menu bar.
